_note: Proposed by the Wave 2 Leviticus data builder, 2026-11-12. Every `strength` here is a PROPOSAL for Lane to confirm or change; pairs come from the verses (shared words, same beat), the commentary is a pointer only. Spans are English numbering. strength: 3 shared words, 2 same story beat, 1 thematic. All are `echo` pairs: none is proposed as a chiasm ring.

sources.cite: Jeffrey H. Tigay, Deuteronomy, JPS Torah Commentary (Philadelphia: Jewish Publication Society, 1996), Excursus 26, pp. 489–92 (structure of Deut 28), with a cross-reference of Lev 26:19 to Deut 28:23.
sources.what: Pointer: Tigay calls both chapters a 'tokhehah', divides Deut 28 into blessings (1–14) and curses (15–68), and notes the matched six blessings and curses.
sources.boundary_note: Lev 26 is touched in passing there. Pairs and shared words come from the verses.

sources.cite: Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible (morphhb: Westminster Leningrad Codex with Strong's-based lemmas), https://github.com/openscriptures/morphhb, pinned morphhb@2.0.2; English verse numbers via its VerseMap.xml.
sources.what: Every Strong's number in a `shared` entry was found in both cited verses by script.
sources.boundary_note: Lemma overlap shows shared vocabulary, not shared meaning; a shared word can be used in a different sense in each place.

pairs.title: Blessings, then curses: the same shape in two chapters
pairs.strength_why: Same beat across the whole: if you keep the commands, blessings; if you do not, curses in escalating stages.
pairs.note: Lev 26 sets the curses in stages marked 'seven times' (vv. 18, 21, 24, 28); Deut 28 has a longer curse half (15–68) and a hinge at v. 45. Wide pair: the narrower pairs below nest inside it.

pairs.title: If you keep my commands: the blessings
pairs.strength_why: Both open 'if you keep my commandments' and then promise fruit of the field.
pairs.note: Lev 26:4 gives rain 'in its season'; Deut 28:12 opens the sky 'in its season' (same word for season, ʻet).

pairs.title: If you do not listen: the curses open
pairs.strength_why: 'If you will not listen' with commandments and statutes (mitsvah, chuqqah) in the same clause.

pairs.title: Wasting disease and fever
pairs.strength_why: Two rare words, shachepheth and qaddachath, occur together in both verses (two rare words, two occurrences each in the Torah's text we hold).

pairs.title: Struck before your enemies; flight
pairs.strength_why: Strike (nagaph), flee (nus) and enemy (oyev) in one verse each; both carry a number of ways or times: seven.
pairs.note: Lev 26:17 has them flee 'when none pursues' (and again in 26:36–37); Deut 28:25 has them flee 'seven ways' from the one enemy they came out against 'one way'.

pairs.title: Sky of iron, earth of bronze
pairs.strength_why: Sky, iron and earth in the same image (bronze is a different word in each); Tigay cross-references the two verses.
pairs.note: The metals trade places (and 'bronze' is nechushah in Lev, nechoshet in Deut): iron for the sky and bronze for the earth in Lev 26:19; bronze for the sky and iron for the earth in Deut 28:23.

pairs.title: Plague, pestilence
pairs.strength_why: 'Blows' (makkah) in Lev 26:21 and in Deut 28:59, 61; 'pestilence' (deber) in Lev 26:25 and Deut 28:21.
pairs.note: Lev 26:21 'seven times more plagues' against Deut 28:59–61 'extraordinary plagues' (outside this pair's span, listed for Lane).

pairs.title: They eat the flesh of their sons and daughters
pairs.strength_why: Eat, flesh, sons and daughters in one clause each.
pairs.note: Deut 28:53–57 extends the scene at length (siege, the tender woman); Lev 26:29 gives it one verse.

pairs.title: Scattered among the nations
pairs.strength_why: Same beat, exile among other peoples; no distinctive word is shared (Lev 26:33 'nations' gôyim, Deut 28:64 'peoples').
